stories.title: Michigan senator flags power and water risks from incoming data centers
stories.dek: A state senator is alerting local officials that new data centers could drive up electricity rates and strain water supplies in Michigan suburbs. Communities without strong local rules may end up subsidizing the facilities through higher utility bills. The warning targets growing interest in data-center sites across metro Detroit and surrounding counties.
stories.source_title: State senator warns communities about data centers - C&G Newspapers

stories.title: Ypsilanti Data Center Plan Spotlights Water and Power Tradeoffs
stories.dek: EMU hydrogeologist Christopher Gellasch said closed-loop cooling can reuse groundwater without warming the subsurface, while activist Peter Sinclair noted possible new energy infrastructure as a community benefit.

stories.title: Mason County questions if local grid can handle data center surge
stories.dek: Western Michigan utilities face rising demand from proposed AI facilities that could strain transmission lines and raise rates for homes and factories. Mason County residents are asking whether new power plants or upgrades will be needed and who pays. The discussion ties directly to whether data centers can locate there without blackouts or higher bills.
stories.source_title: Does western Michigan - and Mason County - have the power? - Shoreline Media Group

stories.title: AG Nessel demands answers from PSC on data center power deals
stories.dek: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel is pressing the Public Service Commission to justify how it handles surging electricity demand from proposed data centers. Residents could face higher utility bills if regulators approve large new loads without stronger oversight. The move signals growing political pushback against unchecked data center growth across the state.
stories.source_title: Nessel wants to hold PSC 'accountable' in fight against data center - The Detroit News

stories.title: OpenAI steps in after Michigan water system hack tied to data-center growth
stories.dek: OpenAI is offering Michigan state officials help hardening cybersecurity on water utilities that supply cooling for planned data centers. The offer follows a recent attack that exposed vulnerabilities in systems already under strain from AI power and water demands. Michigan readers should watch because any new data-center cluster will rely on the same utilities now being targeted.
stories.source_title: OpenAI offers to strengthen Michigan cybersecurity after water infrastructure attack - Detroit Free Press

stories.title: Michigan firm pitches on-site power to dodge grid delays for AI campuses
stories.dek: A local company says it can deliver the massive electricity loads AI data centers need without waiting on utility upgrades. The approach mirrors tactics already used elsewhere and could accelerate projects across the state. It also raises fresh questions about emissions, noise, and who pays when the grid is already strained.
stories.source_title: Elon Musk Found A Way Around The Grid. A Michigan Company Says It Can, Too - MITechNews

stories.title: Detroit drafts data center rules after report flags power strain
stories.dek: City planners released a new assessment showing data centers could add hundreds of megawatts of demand on an already tight grid. Residents 30 miles away in suburbs served by DTE will see higher bills if the load is not managed. The rules would set size limits and require developers to pay for grid upgrades.
stories.source_title: Detroit weighs data center rules as report drops amid growing concerns - The Detroit News

stories.title: Dowagiac neighbors say data center noise runs nonstop
stories.dek: A Cass County facility operates around the clock and residents describe the sound as constant and disturbing. The complaint highlights real-world quality-of-life costs that arrive with data-center projects even after they are built. Local officials have no immediate fix, leaving nearby homeowners to absorb the impact.
stories.source_title: A Dowagiac Data Center Runs 24/7 And Neighbors Say It Screams Like A Demon - NewsBreak: Local News & Alerts

stories.title: Pittsfield Township tightens data center zoning to curb sprawl
stories.dek: Pittsfield Township is drafting zoning changes aimed at data centers after residents raised alarms over noise, traffic and power demand. The rules would affect future projects near Ann Arbor and could set a template for other Washtenaw County townships. Local taxpayers may face higher utility rates if large facilities strain the grid without new safeguards.
stories.source_title: Pittsfield Township considering zoning amendments to address data centers - WEMU

stories.title: Monroe Twp moves to kill $300M lawsuit over its data center ban
stories.dek: Monroe Township wants a federal judge to toss a $300 million suit filed by a data-center developer after the township banned new facilities. The case centers on whether local governments can block projects that would draw massive power and water loads. Residents 30 miles away in southeast Michigan have a direct stake in whether the ban holds or gets overturned in court.
stories.source_title: Monroe Township has requested the dismissal of a $300 million lawsuit against its data center ban - Inquirer.com

stories.title: Data center opponent defeats incumbent in Michigan House primary
stories.dek: A candidate who campaigned against data center growth won a Democratic primary for state House in Michigan. The victory highlights growing voter pushback on power and water demands from these projects. It shifts the local fight into the state legislature for the affected district.
stories.source_title: This Data Center Foe Just Won His Democratic House Primary in Michigan - Mother Jones

national.title: Data centers advance rapidly as regulators scramble for rules
national.dek: Across the U.S., officials race to impose guardrails on power-hungry facilities while communities push back on incentives and impacts.
